reference: GNU coreutils join invoked by the harness with Bash as the reference shell, LC_ALL=C, and matching fixture files. For runnable parity cases, GNU join status, stdout bytes, stderr policy, and resulting fixture trees are compared with the candidate. Bash type/help checks use documented builtin metadata contracts.
coverage: Bash help metadata and documented join options
Default inner join output and duplicate-key Cartesian products
Selected key columns and a single-byte field separator
Unmatched rows, formatted output, and empty or missing field replacement
Unmatched-only modes for both input files
Automatic output layout from first records
Explicit sorted-input validation and failure status
exclusions: Locale-specific collation outside C, resource scaling, and interactive shell behavior are not covered.
Held-producer/FIFO blocking behavior and exact output-failure diagnostic wording are not covered.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash resolves join as a loadable builtin even though candidate execution has an empty PATH.
Verify Bash help exposes a nonempty join synopsis and the documented header and order-check options; stdout is a fixed summary of those independently documented metadata checks.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help join) || exit 1
[[ -n $help_text ]] || exit 2
[[ $help_text == *"join [-i] [-1 N]"* ]] || exit 3
[[ $help_text == *--header* && $help_text == *--check-order* ]] || exit 4
printf 'join help contract available\n'

cases.purpose: Compare the default inner join across two sorted keys, including the GNU-required Cartesian product for duplicate keys.
cases.script:
printf 'a L1
a L2
b L3
' > left
printf 'a R1
a R2
b R3
c R4
' > right
join left right

cases.purpose: Compare -1/-2 key selection with colon-separated fields and verify default output retains non-key fields in file order.
cases.script:
printf 'L0:a:x
L1:b:y
L2:c:z
' > left
printf 'R0:a:p
R1:c:q
R2:d:r
' > right
join -t : -1 2 -2 2 left right

cases.purpose: Compare both-side unmatched output with an explicit field list, checking replacement of empty and absent output fields using -e.
cases.script:
printf 'a:L:
b:B:left
' > left
printf 'a:R:right
c:C:
' > right
join -t : -a 1 -a 2 -e _ -o 0,1.2,2.2,1.3,2.3 left right

cases.purpose: Compare -v1 and -v2 output for records that occur in only one input while common keys are omitted.
cases.script:
printf 'a A
b B
d D
' > left
printf 'a X
c C
d Y
' > right
join -v 1 left right
join -v 2 left right

cases.purpose: Compare GNU ignore-case key matching for sorted ASCII keys with different capitalization.
cases.script:
printf 'A left-one
b left-two
' > left
printf 'a right-one
B right-two
' > right
join -i left right

cases.purpose: Compare GNU header handling: first records are emitted as labels even when their key fields differ, then ordinary records are joined.
cases.script:
printf 'key left-label
a L
' > left
printf 'other right-label
a R
' > right
join --header left right

cases.purpose: Compare -o auto layout inferred from each first record, including later short rows and unmatched rows padded with -e.
cases.script:
printf 'a L1 x
a L2
z L3 q
' > left
printf 'a R1 y
m R2
z R3 w
' > right
join -o auto -a 1 -a 2 -e _ left right

cases.purpose: Compare reading standard input as the first and second file operand using only relative fixture files and shell redirection.
cases.script:
printf 'a L
b M
' > left
printf 'a R
b S
' > right
join - right < left
join left - < right

cases.purpose: A closed stdout is an output failure with status 1; stderr remains open and diagnostics remain in the raw evidence.
cases.script:
printf 'a L\n' > left
printf 'a R\n' > right
join left right >&-

cases.purpose: Compare explicit GNU sorted-input checking on a disorder reached while both inputs remain; the join invocation must emit its matched prefix and exit with status 1.
cases.script:
printf 'a A\nc C\nb B\n' > left
printf 'a X\nc Y\nz Z\n' > right
set +e
join --check-order left right
rc=$?
set -e
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]] || exit 99
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: NUL bytes and trailing CR remain field bytes; each invocation starts with fresh stdin state in both positions.
cases.script:
printf 'a L\000x\r\nb M\n' > left
printf 'a R\000y\r\nb N\n' > right
join - right < left
join - right < left
join left - < right
